title: Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan: Enrollment and the Number of Plans a Worker May Hold
content:
## Rule

A worker may hold up to **2** Paystride Earned Wage Access Plans at once, counting every plan whose status is not closed. A second plan exists only for a second employer, because each plan belongs to one employer program agreement. A worker may not hold a second plan that is not closed under the same employer program agreement.

Enrollment is accepted only while the employer's Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement status is live.

Re-enrollment under the same employer program agreement is accepted only when the tier's re-enrollment cooldown in calendar days has passed since the closed date of the worker's most recent closed plan under that agreement. Calendar days are counted from the day after that closed date, so the first permitted re-enrollment date is the closed date plus the cooldown days.

An enrollment that would exceed either limit is refused and the worker uses the plan they already hold.

Every new plan opens in pending activation at Paystride Access Starter with a zero outstanding balance, the employee number, hire date, pay frequency and next payday taken from the employer's payroll file, and the card recovery authorization set to false until the worker grants it.

## What the records must show

| Condition | Evidence | Matched on |
|---|---|---|
| No second open plan under the same agreement | the worker's plans and their statuses (pending activation, active, paused or suspended each count as not closed) | the program agreement of the enrollment |
| Program live | the program agreement's status | the program agreement of the enrollment |
| Re-enrollment cooldown | the closed date of the worker's most recent closed plan under that agreement | the program agreement of the enrollment |

Each of these is read from the system records before the enrollment, never from the worker's statement.

## Cooldown boundary (hypothetical dates)

With a 30-day cooldown and a most recent closed date of 4 March:

- 3 April is the closed date plus 30 days: re-enrollment is accepted on that day (the boundary day satisfies the rule).
- 2 April is one day short: re-enrollment is refused.

## Points of judgement

- Two plans under two different employers' agreements: permitted, as two is the most a worker may hold.
- A third plan while two are not closed: refused.
- A closed plan does not count toward the two.
